questions.question: In the following question, select the odd word pair from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
The pairs "Pedal - Cycle", "Room - House", and "Chapter - Book" represent a part-whole relationship, where the first item is an integral part of the second item:

 
• A pedal is an integral part of a cycle.
 
• A room is an integral part of a house.
 
• A chapter is an integral part of a book.

However, the pair "Fan - Blade" doesn't follow the same pattern. Here, blade is integral part of Fan which should second part not first part.

Therefore, "Fan - Blade" is the odd pair out, as the first item doesn't necessarily include the second item.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All R are P.

II. All P are J.

**Conclusions:**

I. All P are R.

II. All J are P.

III. All R are J.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. All R are P.

II. All P are J.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3302130976cee5b9bc38c9a1c3f40a73c4d5a6b885c7853a283223e945042d79.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All P are R - False (Because, the given statement is All R are P, so some R will be P definitely but All P are R can be possible only).

II. All J are P - False (Because, the given statement is All P are J, so some J will be P definitely but All J are P can be possible only).

III. All R are J - True (Because, All R are P and All P are J, so All R are J).

So, Only conclusion III follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
Words given on the left side of (::) are related with each other by some Logic/Rule /Relation. Select the missing word/word pair on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

Track : Race :: Pitch : ?
questions.solution:
The relationship here is "venue or place : activity conducted".

In the pair "Track : Race", a track is the place or venue where a race is typically conducted.

Following this pattern, a pitch is the place or venue where a game of cricket is typically played. Therefore, "Pitch : Cricket" follows the same relationship.

As for the other options:

 
• Wrestling typically takes place in a ring, not on a pitch.
 
• Chess is played on a board, not a pitch.
 
• Exercise could be conducted in many places, and the term 'pitch' is not typically associated with exercise.

Therefore, "Cricket" is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘BACK’ is coded as ‘2325215’, ‘CAME’ is coded as ‘2125117’. What is the code for ‘GBJH’ in that code language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0270f2b5240d1e3915517248ac98d6d73ad611166857551401277421991a6c6e.png] 

**Logic: Place value of Opposite letter - Positional value of given letter**

‘BACK’ is coded as ‘2325215

B → Y(25) - B(2) = 23

A → Z(26) - A(1) = 25

C → X(24) - C(3) = 21

K → P(16) - K(11) = 5

‘CAME’ is coded as ‘2125117

C → X(24) - C(3) = 21

A → Z(26) - A(1) = 25

M → N(14) - M(13) = 1

E → V(22) - E(5) = 17

Similarly,

G → T (20) - G (7) = 13

B → Y (25) - B (2) = 23

J → Q(17) - J (10) = 7

H → S(19) - H (8) = 11

Hence, the correct answer is **1323711.**

questions.question:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if '+' and ‘×’ are interchanged and also '-' and '÷' are interchanged?

20 ÷ 5 × 10 - 5 + 2 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Given equation: 20 ÷ 5 × 10 - 5 + 2 = ? 

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘×‘ and ‘-’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ 20 - 5 + __**10 ÷ 5**__ × 2 = ? 

⇒ 20 - 5 + **__2__**__** ×**____** 2**__ = ? 

⇒ __**20**__ - 5 __**+ 4**__ = ? 

⇒ __24 - 5__ = 19.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

Turtle : Reptile :: ?
questions.solution:
In the given pair "Turtle : Reptile", a turtle is an example of a reptile. So, we need to find a pair where the second word is the class of the animal, and the first word is an example of that class.

Following this logic:

 
• "Snake : Rodent" is incorrect, as a snake is a reptile, not a rodent.
 
• "Mammal : Man" is incorrect, as according to the given format, the class (mammal) should be in the second place, not the first.
 
• "Lizard : Reptile" is correct, as a lizard is indeed an example of a reptile, which follows the same pattern.
 
• "Mammal : Frog" is incorrect, as a frog is an amphibian, not a mammal.

Therefore, the correct answer is** "3) Lizard : Reptile".**

Logic: (1st number × 3) + 3 = 2nd number.

Now,

For, 9 : 30

⇒ (9 × 3) + 3

⇒ 27 + 3 = 30.

For, 11 : 36

⇒ (11 × 3) + 3

⇒ 33 + 3 = 36.

Similarly, for **13** ∶ ?

**⇒ (13 × 3) + 3**

**⇒ 39 + 3 = 42.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
